Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
- Summary of key findings consistent with a developing anxiety/mood disorder: 
  - Onset ~2 months ago, coinciding with a new, stressful job
  - Persistent morning anxiety about leaving home; sleep disturbance with little restorative sleep
  - Palpitations described as irregular and distressing, often in the morning
  - Daytime fatigue, anhedonia, reduced interest in activities, social withdrawal
  - Functionally impairing at work and in social life; no active suicidality reported
- Likely contributing/related diagnoses (based on DDx and transcript): 
  - Adjustment Disorder with Anxiety — High likelihood
  - Major Depressive Disorder with anxious distress — Moderate likelihood
  - Generalized Anxiety Disorder (or mixed anxiety/depressive features) — Moderate likelihood
- Notes on consistency or conflict: No conflicts between transcript and DDx identified

Management Plan
- Primary actions today:
  - Initiate access to talking therapy (CBT-type) via self-referral; provide NHS resources/link
  - Basic blood tests ordered to rule out medical triggers for palpitations and sleep disturbance; GP follow-up in 1 week after results
  - Sleep hygiene and sleep pattern guidance to be added to notes
  - Reassure that medication is not first-line at this stage unless symptoms worsen or fail to improve
- Additional considerations:
  - Consider referral for allied health support if ongoing impairment persists (e.g., психологical therapy; ongoing monitoring)
  - Encourage ongoing contact with supportive family; assess safety and escalation if suicidality emerges
  - Reassess in a follow-up visit after investigations and therapy engagement
